nodes.title: Current-owner places and absolute height normalization
nodes.statement: For a number field K of degree d, identify the legacy InfinitePlace K ⊕ FinitePlace K with GlobalNumberFields.Place K by swapping the summands and identifying finite places with height-one prime ideals. Current infinite factors are v(x)^{mult(v)} and finite factors are the adic norms. Raise each current factor to 1/d to obtain the normalized factors used by H₂ and H_Q. The product formula is preserved. In E/K, the factor over w|v carries exponent d(w|v)=[E_w:K_v]/[E:K]. In particular H(x)=Height.mulHeight(x)^{1/d} for a nonzero tuple and h(x)=Height.logHeight(x)/d.
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the native finite-place equivalence; the infinite factor retains its multiplicity before the degree root.
Use the product formula and the local-degree sum over each v to prove invariance under finite extension. This is the compatibility needed by the parent height, not a new place definition.
acceptance: For K=ℚ the root exponent is 1; at a complex place of a quadratic field it is 2/2, not 1/2.
The complex squared factor is not treated as an AbsoluteValue: its triangle estimate has exponent 2/d.

nodes.title: Local exterior-power norm and determinant bounds
nodes.statement: For a p×n matrix of vectors over a normalized local field, the sup norm of its p-minors is at most the product of column sup norms at a nonarchimedean place; the Euclidean norm of those minors is at most the product of the p Euclidean vector norms at an archimedean place. Consequently H₂(span(x₁,…,x_p))≤∏ H₂(x_i) for independent vectors, and the wedge-coordinate sup version has the factor p^{p/2} when each input uses a coordinate sup norm.
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: At an archimedean place apply Cauchy–Binet to the Gram determinant and Hadamard; at finite places use the ultrametric determinant expansion.
Multiply with normalized local weights. The archimedean weights sum to 1, which gives one global p^{p/2}, rather than a power depending on K.
acceptance: For p=1 this is equality.
For p=n the wedge is a determinant, and its projective height is 1.

nodes.title: Plücker duality and orthogonal complement heights
nodes.statement: For a k-dimensional K-subspace U⊂Kⁿ, the signed complementary-minor map identifies its Plücker vector with that of the annihilator U⊥ for the standard bilinear pairing. Thus H₂(U⊥)=H₂(U); also H₂(U)=1 for k=0,n. This statement concerns bilinear annihilators over K, with Hermitian norms only after embedding at infinity.
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Choose an invertible basis minor and row-reduce. The kernel matrix has complementary minors equal up to one common nonzero scalar and signs.
Signed coordinate permutation preserves every local sup or Euclidean norm; projective invariance cancels the common scalar.
acceptance: For a rational line generated by (2,3), its perpendicular line generated by (−3,2) has the same H₂=√13.

nodes.title: Intersection and sum inequality for subspace heights
nodes.statement: For subspaces U,V⊂Kⁿ, H₂(U∩V) H₂(U+V)≤H₂(U)H₂(V). This includes nontrivial intersections, and is stronger than applying the exterior product bound only in the disjoint case.
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Use a common basis A of U∩V and complements B,C. At each archimedean place pass to the quotient by span(A); Gram–Schmidt gives volume(A,B,C) volume(A)≤volume(A,B)volume(A,C).
At a finite place use a unit minor of A after scaling and elimination; the induced quotient sup norm gives the corresponding nonarchimedean determinant inequality.
Multiply local inequalities, cancel the projective scalars, and use the product formula. The lecture notes quote the inequality; the local quotient proof is the required development.
acceptance: If U⊂V both sides are equal.
In ℚ³, U=span(e₁,e₂) and V=span(e₁,e₂+e₃) give 1·1≤1·√2.

nodes.title: Northcott for fixed-degree subspaces
nodes.statement: For n,k,D and B fixed, only finitely many k-subspaces U⊂Q̄ⁿ with [field of definition of U:ℚ]≤D and H₂(U)≤B exist. A Plücker chart with a nonzero coordinate makes every ratio a scalar of degree≤D and absolute multiplicative height≤B; the injective Plücker map then reduces to fixed-degree scalar Northcott.
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Choose one of finitely many nonzero Plücker coordinates and divide by it.
Bound the heights of coordinate ratios by the Plücker sup height, which is≤H₂; use the parent fixed-degree scalar Northcott and Plücker reconstruction.

nodes.title: Primitive Plücker coordinates and rational covolume
nodes.statement: For a rational k-subspace U⊂ℚⁿ, L=U∩ℤⁿ is saturated and has rank k. Every specified ℤ-basis b of L extends to a basis of ℤⁿ, hence the gcd of the k-minors of b is 1. Therefore H₂(U)=√det(Gram(b))=covol(L) in U⊗ℝ. This constructs the lattice and proves primitivity, rather than assuming an arbitrary integral basis is primitive.
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Saturation follows from m x∈U⇒x∈U for nonzero integer m. Use the prescribed-basis extension theorem, and expand determinant±1 along the first k columns to obtain an integral combination of minors equal to±1.
Finite local height factors are then 1; Cauchy–Binet supplies the infinite factor.
acceptance: For the line (2,3) the primitive basis gives √13; using twice this vector without dividing its common factor would wrongly give 2√13.

nodes.title: Full S-unit logarithmic image
nodes.statement: Let S contain all infinite places and finitely many finite places of K. The map u↦(log|u|_v)_{v∈S}, with degree-normalized factors, has torsion kernel and image a full lattice in Σ_v z_v=0. In particular every vector of that hyperplane is within a K,S-dependent bounded sup distance of some unit logarithm. Native finite generation alone does not imply fullness.
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Use ordinary Dirichlet for the infinite-place kernel and principal powers of the finitely many prime ideals in S to obtain independent finite valuation directions.
The class group finiteness/principal-power contract is requested from the lower-tier global number-field owner; do not import the higher-tier K-theory rank plan.
The product formula places the image in the hyperplane. The obtained independent directions give a full lattice; a bounded fundamental parallelepiped gives the approximation.
acceptance: For ℚ with S={∞,p}, the logarithmic image is ℤ(log p,−log p).
For imaginary quadratic K and only infinite places, the hyperplane and free unit rank are both zero.

nodes.title: Absolute rescaling with one distinguished place
nodes.statement: Let A_v>0 equal 1 outside a finite set containing all infinite places, with A=∏A_v≥1; fix v₀ and ε>0. There are a finite extension E/K and β∈E* with |β|_w≤A_v^{d(w|v)} for w|v≠v₀ and |β|_w≤((1+ε)A_{v₀}/A)^{d(w|v₀)} for w|v₀. The variant without a distinguished place uses ∏A_v>1 and gives |β|_w≤A_v^{d(w|v)} everywhere.
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Approximate a large multiple of the balanced target vector of logarithms by the S-unit lattice. Reserve the positive log(1+ε) margin at v₀ and enough negative margin elsewhere to absorb the bounded error.
Adjoin a k-th root of that unit; divide all errors by k and check the local-degree weights. This is why the scalar may require a finite extension.
acceptance: When A=1 and all A_v=1 one may take β=1.
A zero ε boundary is not inferred from approximation.

nodes.title: Unitary symmetric-power metric
nodes.statement: On Symʳ(Kᵐ), write v=Σ_{|I|=r} a_I e^I. At an archimedean place use ‖v‖²=Σ |a_I|²/binomial(r;I); use the dual norm Σ binomial(r;I)|b_I|² on homogeneous polynomial coefficients. At finite places keep the prescribed adelic sup norm. This is the symmetric-tensor metric transported from the invariant symmetric subspace of the tensor power; plain coefficient Euclidean norm is not unitary-invariant.
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Average tensor words with each given multiplicity. Their number is binomial(r;I), so the symmetric average has squared norm 1/binomial(r;I).

The dual pairing gives the reciprocal coefficient weights. Compare to coefficient sup/Euclidean norms using explicit multinomial factors; the later absolute-basis argument must be checked in the erratum.
acceptance: The quadratic cross-term has squared weight 1/2; verify invariance on the displayed 45-degree rotation and dual weight 2.

nodes.title: From corrected absolute bases to twisted Minkowski
nodes.statement: Assume the corrected absolute small-basis theorem for adelic Hermitian spaces, with the Roy–Thunder determinant/metric conventions. Apply it to the n coordinate forms at every place, then pass to the algebraic-closure infima. The resulting statement is the parent absolute Minkowski theorem n^{−n/2}Δ Q^{−α}≤∏_{i=1}^n λ_i(Q)≤2^{n(n−1)/2}Δ Q^{−α}, with α=Σ_{v,i}c_{iv}. The lower bound follows directly from local determinants and does not need the unread erratum.

proofSteps: For independent nearly minimizing vectors bound each local determinant by the product of local form maxima, with the normalized archimedean factor n^{n/2}; multiply to obtain the lower inequality.

For the upper inequality match the adelic twisted box to the corrected absolute-basis theorem and rescale via the preceding lemma. A fixed-field Minkowski theorem is insufficient because λ_i is taken over Q̄.
The upper-bound source is a recorded gap until the full 1999 erratum proof is obtained and its constants propagated.

nodes.title: Successive infima, gap subspaces and Galois descent
nodes.statement: For a twisted height H_Q satisfying the parent finite-support, field-extension and Galois compatibility conditions, 0<λ₁(Q)≤⋯≤λ_n(Q)<∞. For every ε>0 choose independent x_i with H_Q(x_i)≤(1+ε)λ_i. If λ_k<λ_{k+1}, the span of vectors with H_Q(x)<λ_{k+1} has dimension k and is K-defined. Comparing two form systems differing at at most R places gives the coordinate bounds of EF Lemmas 9.3–9.4 using their local Cramer constants; no attainment over Q̄ is asserted.
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Positivity and finiteness follow from determinant bounds and a coordinate basis; the definition of the infimum gives independent near minimizers.
Below a genuine adjacent gap the span is independent of the threshold and has dimension k. Galois invariance of H_Q makes this span stable, hence K-defined by the parent descent input.
Use inverse matrices and the local Cramer bounds to compare systems, then multiply; retain local determinant factors rather than pretending arbitrary changes of basis are isometric.
acceptance: Use strict adjacent gaps only. A span of near minimizers must be independent of their choices before invoking Galois descent.

nodes.title: Restriction heights and subspace-height lower bounds
nodes.statement: For k-dimensional T, choose a nonzero basis minor and an isomorphism φ:Q̄ᵏ→T whose selected coordinate minor is the identity. Restricted forms have exterior coefficient heights bounded by √binomial(n,k) H_L H₂(T), with the minimum nonzero restricted determinant carried explicitly. If λ_k(Q)≤Q^{−δ} and λ_{k+1}(Q)>λ_k(Q), the corresponding gap subspace satisfies H₂(T)≥Q^{δ/(3Rⁿ)} in the semistable setting of EF Lemma 10.3.
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Coordinate projections of φ are bounded by complementary minors; multiply the restricted-minor bounds to obtain Lemma 10.2 with its actual minimum determinant denominator.
Combine the determinant lower bound, the restricted weights and semistability w(T)≤0. If H₂(T) were smaller than the stated power, the k-minimum bound would contradict this product estimate.
acceptance: The estimate requires the semistable assumptions; a positive-weight exceptional subspace is not a counterexample to the conditional statement.

nodes.title: Nearly minimizing bases with concentrated archimedean slack
nodes.statement: Fix v₀ and ε>0. Independent near minimizers can be individually rescaled so that |L_{iv}(x_j)|_v≤n^{−s(v)}Q^{c_{iv}} away from v₀, while at v₀ the bounds are ((1+ε)nλ_j(Q))^{d(w|v₀)}Q^{c_{iw}}. Here s(v)=[K_v:ℝ]/[K:ℚ] at infinity and zero at finite places; after extension the same exponents are multiplied by d(w|v).
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Take a common finite field for the independent vectors. For each vector set A_v from its actual local twisted maximum and apply distinguished-place rescaling.
The product of the A_v is its twisted height; use the near-minimum bound. The independent scalar multiplications preserve independence.
acceptance: The distinguished place is finite and has zero weights and coordinate forms. Multiply the rescaling factors to recover the global near-minimum bound.

nodes.title: Adelic approximation of elimination coefficients
nodes.statement: Given algebraic θ₁,…,θ_{t−1}, a distinguished place v₀ and ε>0, there are algebraic γ₁,…,γ_t with γ_t≠0: |γ_i|_v≤t^{−s(v)} at archimedean v≠v₀ and≤1 at finite v≠v₀; at v₀, |γ_i−θ_iγ_t|_w≤1 and |γ_t|_w≤((1+ε)^t2^{t²})^{d(w|v₀)}. The formulation is after a finite extension containing all coefficients.

proofSteps: Apply absolute Minkowski to a unipotent system with last coordinate γ_t and the error forms γ_i−θ_iγ_t.
Choose the first nonzero vector after absolute rescaling; if γ_t=0 the remaining coordinates have a strictly too small global product, contradicting the product formula.
Track the archimedean factors and use the generous 2^{t²} bound for the successive-minima product.

nodes.title: Davenport elimination along a Galois-defined flag
nodes.statement: In the parent semistable setting, with distinguished nonarchimedean v₀ where c_{iv₀}=0 and L_{iv₀}=X_i, fix Q≥1. Choose ε>0 with (1+ε)²λ_i<λ_{i+1} at every strict gap and n·2^{n²}(1+ε)^{n+1}<3^{n²}, and independent g_i with H_Q(g_i)≤(1+ε/2)λ_i. There are a finite extension E/K, a permutation π and a basis h_j preserving every initial span of the g_j, such that |L_{iw}(h_j)|_w≤n^{−s(w)}Q^{c_{iw}} for w not over v₀, and |L_{π(i),w}(h_j)|_w≤[3^{n²}min(λ_i,λ_j)]^{d(w|v₀)} for w over v₀. Here s(w) is the normalized infinite local degree and zero at finite places.
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Select pivots in K-defined annihilators of the flag blocks; use Gaussian elimination in increasing block order.
Approximate each elimination coefficient by the preceding adelic lemma, preserving previous pivots. Multiply the local error bounds and sum the geometric losses to obtain 3^{n²}.

nodes.title: Corrected class-modulus proposition
nodes.statement: Let Q-independent forms M_j have nonzero coefficient rows a_i with trailing support lengths t_i, let T=min(kⁿ,e^{12Σt_i}), ℏ=e^{−6T⁴}, and α_i≠0 algebraic. Each class has a modulus m≥1 with all x congruent modulo m, and some i≠j such that either α_i/α_j is not torsion and h(α_i^m/α_j^m)≥ℏ, or it is torsion and ord(α_i^m/α_j^m)≤ℏ^{−1}. nodes.title: Finite obstruction to lowering a progression count
nodes.statement: For Z⊂ℤ a finite union of two-sided arithmetic progressions and singletons, let ν(Z) be its least number of such pieces. There is a finite T⊂ℤ outside Z such that every finite union Z′⊃Z with Z′∩T=∅ satisfies ν(Z′)≥ν(Z). This lower bound, rather than equality for arbitrary supersets, is the contract needed for specialization.
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Choose a minimal representation with isolated points Z₁ and periodic part Z₂. For each pair of isolated points, exclude one nonzero-set point on the progression through that pair, so a progression avoiding T contains at most one isolated point.
If Z₂ has period q, put ℓ=qν(Z). In a translated interval of length qℓ disjoint from Z₁, exclude all points outside Z₂. Every progression of modulus≤ℓ avoiding this finite set lies in Z₂.

Suppose Z′ had fewer than ν(Z) pieces. Replace progressions disjoint from Z₂ by their at most one isolated point; enlarge the small-modulus progressions inside Z₂ to moduli dividing q. Their periodic union must fill Z₂: otherwise its density is short by at least 1/q, and the remaining fewer than ν(Z) progressions each have density<1/ℓ.

The periodic pieces therefore need at least ν(Z₂) pieces, and every remaining piece covers at most one isolated point. Their total is at least ν(Z), a contradiction. This proves the stated lower bound.
acceptance: For Z={0} one can take T empty; Z′={0,1} shows why the conclusion is a lower bound rather than equality.
For Z=2ℤ∪3ℤ, the obstruction protects a least cover by two independent moduli; it does not prescribe one common modulus.

nodes.title: Refined counts for multiple-root recurrences
nodes.statement: Let a nonzero recurrence over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field have minimal order t≥1, k distinct nonzero roots and maximum root multiplicity a. Its integer zero set is a union of at most exp(exp(70t)) arithmetic progressions, including singletons. If no quotient of distinct roots is a root of unity, it has at most (8k^a)^{8k^{6a}} zeros, also≤exp(32a k^{6a}log k) for k≥2. For k=1 there are at most a−1 zeros. No common progression modulus is required.
hypotheses: All fields, dimensions, normalizations and strict inequalities are as specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Expand the coefficient polynomials in a Q-basis to get independent forms; fewer than a exceptional indices make all coefficient polynomials vanish.
On a class x=x₀+my, replace roots by α_i^m. In the torsion case split into at most ℏ^{−1} residue classes and merge equal powered roots, decreasing t.

In the non-torsion case use degree lowering. An infinite progression from a lower-degree auxiliary equation need not be wholly inside the original zero set: restrict the original equation to it and merge equal powered roots before the second induction. This explains the square in Z(t,T).
The general induction uses Z(t,T)=(8T)^{(2^t−1)8T⁵}; the nondegenerate induction uses (8T)^{8T⁵t} without the square. Substitute T≤e^{12t} or T≤k^a respectively.

First transfer the nondegenerate bound to arbitrary characteristic-zero coefficients using Schmidt1999 §2, Lemma 1, pp.246–247. The rank-deficiency equations for a nonzero polynomial vector vanishing on its whole zero set define a variety over ℚ, even for an infinite zero set, by Noetherianity. On a ℚ-irreducible component of degree A, generic rational linear sections give an algebraic point of degree≤A outside any finite union of proper closed subsets.

The root-ratio hypersurface for exact torsion order m forces point degree≥φ(m). Since φ(m)→∞, only finitely many such hypersurfaces can contain a point of degree≤A. Exclude these finitely many and the zero-root locus before taking the section. Solve the remaining nonzero coefficient kernel over its number field. This preserves all original zeros and nondegeneracy, without claiming to preserve every nonzero value.

For general roots, let q be the lcm of the orders of torsion root ratios. On each residue modulo q merge equal powered roots. Either the merged coefficient polynomials all vanish identically, yielding a whole progression, or their non-torsion ratios and the just-transferred nondegenerate theorem give finitely many zeros. This establishes qualitative SML within this proof, before using it in specialization.

Apply the finite-progression-obstruction node to that zero set. The parent specialization lemma, with inverses of the roots, leading coefficients and finitely many values indexed by T adjoined, preserves the order and those nonzero values; every original zero is preserved by the ring homomorphism. The specialized zero set contains the original and avoids T, so its least progression count is at least the original count. Apply the algebraic general bound. The finitely generated coefficient field embeds in ℂ, extending the argument to any characteristic-zero field.
acceptance: For (1−ζ_r^x)(1−ζ_s^x), gcd(r,s)=1, the zero set is rℤ∪sℤ and need not admit a small equal-modulus representation.
For (x−3)2^x, k=1,a=2 and the zero set is the singleton {3}.
